title: Historical TID ODE blow-up-time certificate
asserted_expression: For y' = a y^2 - b y with a>0, b>0 and y(t0)=y0>b/a, the candidate solution has a future denominator singularity at T*=t0+Log[a y0/(a y0-b)]/b.
wolfram_code: sol=(b Exp[b t0] y0)/(b Exp[b t]-a Exp[b t] y0+a Exp[b t0] y0); tstar=t0+Log[a y0/(a y0-b)]/b; asm=a>0&&b>0&&y0>b/a; odeOK=FullSimplify[D[sol,t]==a sol^2-b sol,Assumptions->asm]; icOK=FullSimplify[(sol/.t->t0)==y0,Assumptions->asm]; denOK=FullSimplify[(Denominator[Together[sol]]/.t->tstar)==0,Assumptions->asm]; futureOK=FullSimplify[tstar>t0,Assumptions->asm]; ExportString[<|"exact"->ToString[InputForm[tstar]],"decimal"->N[tstar/.{a->2,b->1,y0->1,t0->0},12],"equals_asserted"->TrueQ[odeOK&&icOK&&denOK&&futureOK]|>,"RawJSON"]
does_not_establish: This verifies only the displayed scalar ODE solution certificate and its future denominator singularity under the stated assumptions. It does not establish that the TID variable Delta-f obeys this ODE, does not connect the ODE to Navier-Stokes norms, and does not prove finite-time blow-up for Navier-Stokes.
